idiom_name: abstract type member visitor with stackable traits for extensions (Zenger-Odersky encoding)
implementation_notes: Scala's published encoding of this pattern (Zenger and Odersky's expression-problem report) keeps elements open by abstracting over the visitor type: an element trait declares an abstract type member for its visitor plus the accept method, a datatype extension refines that type member covariantly to the extended visitor trait, and existing operations are reused through mixin composition rather than casts, so a new variant is added by extending the element trait, refining the visitor trait with its visit method and overriding the default case to re-dispatch. Scala 3 offers two local answers that often beat the encoding: `sealed` hierarchies with exhaustive pattern matching when the variant set can be closed in one file, and given-instance type classes when operations must be added without touching the data at all - the docs note that 'instances for type classes can be defined anywhere', which is the functional side of the expression problem. Keep the visitor encoding when the same structure must support both new variants and new operations across separately compiled modules and the type-level guarantee is worth the machinery.
pitfalls: The encoding rides on path-dependent abstract types: a visitor class must be annotated with the element trait's visitor bound and instantiated through a factory, otherwise accept type-checks as an unchecked cast and the extension is unsafe.

Extensions compose by mixin linearisation, which silently decides precedence when two extensions define the same member, and `super` calls are order-sensitive; a conflicting member is a compile error only when the traits are mixed in directly.
Refining the abstract visitor type covariantly forces every existing operation to be restated in the extension branch, so the boilerplate grows with the number of operations times extensions.
For a closed variant set the language has a smaller answer (sealed traits plus match, or given instances), so the visitor protocol is only justified while the hierarchy must stay open.
